title: Playbook vignettes — contrarian angles for five verticals
content:
Purpose and constraints:
This is a working set of short vignettes and contrarian messaging angles for five priority verticals: fintech, healthcare, legal, enterprise SaaS, gov/defense. The intent is not to be final copy — it’s a rapid ideation doc for SDRs, solutions, and content to test 2–3 week experiments. Keep ideas small and measurable.

Format used for each vertical (keeps us comparable):
- TL;DR positioning line
- Primary buyer / persona + job impact
- 3 core problems we can credibly solve (ranked)
- Contrarian angle (framing that breaks usual vendor noise)
- Proof points / evidence we can use (internal metrics, feature hooks)
- Most relevant competitors and their weakness to exploit
- Quick tactical plays (email subject line, landing page hook, workshop topic)
- Risks / likely objections + quick rebuttals
- Pilot metrics to track (leading and lagging)

1) Fintech (retail & payments platforms)
TL;DR: Make inference economics a predictable unit of product velocity — not a mystery cloud bill.
Persona: Head of Payments / ML Engineering — cares about consistent throughput for fraud models, throttling during spikes, and predictable cost per decision.
Core problems:
- Token/compute cost unpredictability across bursty traffic
- Latency SLO violations at peak (user checkout)
- Compliance/data isolation for transaction data
Contrarian angle: Don’t lead with model quality — lead with 'cost per approval' and 'probability of checkout abandonment prevented'. Finance and product care about dollars/ops more than tokens.
Proof points:
- Dedicated capacity guarantees + example 95th p latency from internal benchmark (tweak for demo)
- Case study sketch: payments startup reduced LLM inference spend by 37% using Redwood batching + prefix cache (internal test)
Competitors: Generic cloud endpoints, vendor X LLM-API, self-hosted runtime stacks.
- Weakness: many sell model access; no clear cost-conversion story tied to product metrics.
Tactical plays:
- Email subject: "Reduce approval latency spikes without buying more GPUs"
- 30-minute workshop: "From tokens to dollars: rethinking LLM economics for payments teams"
- Landing page: calculator that converts tokens->cost->checkout-impact (interactive).
Risks + rebuttals:
- Objection: "We already run local infra" → Rebuttal: migration risk, but show fast PoC with traffic replay + deterministic rollbacks.
Pilot metrics:
- Leading: reduction in 95th-p token latency, # of model fallbacks avoided
- Lagging: $/approved decision, checkout abandonment delta

2) Healthcare (clinical decision support vendors)
TL;DR: Treat inference like medical equipment — validated, auditable, and privately controlled.
Persona: Head of Product (Healthcare) / Security & Compliance lead
Core problems:
- Auditing model outputs & provenance for regulators
- Controlled environments for PHI and on-prem requirements
- Maintaining model behavior stability across updates
Contrarian angle: Instead of promising better accuracy, promise auditable traceability and reproducible model rollouts. Clinicians and hospitals want defensible processes first.
Proof points:
- Private deployment + KMS/HSM integrations (talk point)
- A sample audit log template and provenance report (deliverable for pilots)
Competitors: Platform vendors that only offer hosted SaaS inference, managed vendors without on-prem option.
- Weakness: lack of end-to-end auditability and keys under customer control.
Tactical plays:
- Workshop: "Build an audit trail for every clinical inference — 90 min"
- One-pager: audit-ready deployment checklist for clinical pilots
Risks + rebuttals:
- Objection: "Too heavy/slow to deploy" → Rebuttal: start with VPC mode + limited-scope EHR replay pilot to show performance and auditability without full on-prem.
Pilot metrics:
- Leading: time-to-first-auditable-inference, number of provenance fields captured
- Lagging: pilot approval from risk/compliance committee

3) Legal (contract review & eDiscovery tools)
TL;DR: Make model outputs explainable — reduce legal risk while raising throughput.
Persona: Head of Product / Legal Ops manager
Core problems:
- High variance in false positives/negatives from black-box models
- Requirement to attach explicit rationale for each recommendation
- Chain-of-custody concerns in eDiscovery workflows
Contrarian angle: Position Redwood as 'explainability-as-infrastructure' — not just faster review, but defensible automation with evidence artifacts baked into the output.
Proof points:
- Function-calling + structured outputs for deterministic extraction
- Example policy: automatic citation + paragraph anchors in contract redlines
Competitors: Niche legal AI startups that prioritize accuracy but not operational audit features.
- Weakness: Most can’t produce structured, verifiable output with consistent schema at scale.
Tactical plays:
- Email subject: "Make every automated redline auditable"
- Demo flow: uploaded contract → structured redline + citation pack → exportable evidence bundle
Risks + rebuttals:
- Objection: "We need perfect accuracy for legal tasks" → Rebuttal: show human-in-loop workflows where Redwood reduces review scope while preserving human final authority.
Pilot metrics:
- Leading: % of redlines that include structured citation metadata
- Lagging: time-to-review reduction, legal team satisfaction score

4) Enterprise SaaS (platforms embedding assistant features)
TL;DR: Ship LLM features without binding your product roadmap to one cloud region or one model vendor.
Persona: VP Product / Platform Engineering
Core problems:
- Vendor lock-in with single-model APIs
- Hard to standardize inference behavior across regions/tiers
- Cost & latency unpredictability as feature usage scales
Contrarian angle: Sell the control plane: 'same API, different economics' — let product teams keep features while swapping models or infra without code changes.
Proof points:
- Model pinning + automated fallback policies, A/B rollout tools in Console
- Batching/caching suggestions that map to cost savings per 10k users
Competitors: Cloud model marketplaces, single-API vendors.
- Weakness: lack of deployment parity across hosted/dedicated/private modes.
Tactical plays:
- Landing page: "Swap your model under the hood — zero product changes" (GIF demo)
- Developer workshop: "Pin, roll, fallback — safe model rollouts for product teams"
Risks + rebuttals:
- Objection: "We already solved retries internally" → Rebuttal: show how Redwood routes by policy and reduces product-level complexity.
Pilot metrics:
- Leading: time to integrate SDK + # of routes instrumented
- Lagging: cost delta per MAU after batching config changes

5) Gov/Defense (secure deployments, classified-adjacent)
TL;DR: Defendability and predictable ops > marginal model improvements.
Persona: Program Manager / Security Architect
Core problems:
- Must satisfy procurement/security checkboxes (SLA, logging, KMS)
- Air-gapped or restricted network requirements
- Multi-vendor compliance across supply chain
Contrarian angle: Frame Redwood as a systems-level compliance layer — not an ML vendor. The ask is to be a dependable subsystem within a secure architecture.
Proof points:
- Private deployment architecture drawings + hardened consoles
- STIG-like checklist (draft) and example integration notes for a classified network (sanitize language)
Competitors: Specialized cleared vendors and larger cloud providers with government offerings.
- Weakness: many lack flexible deployment modes that are dev-friendly and observable.
Tactical plays:
- Playbook: procurement-ready spec + sample contract language (security attachments)
- Workshop: "Integrating private inference into a secure architecture — 2hrs"
Risks + rebuttals:
- Objection: "We require cleared personnel / supply chain" → Rebuttal: partner model for cleared ops + phased pilot that limits sensitive traffic.
Pilot metrics:
- Leading: security checklist completion %, time to deploy in VPC
- Lagging: formal authority-to-operate (ATO) progress steps

Cross-vertical notes / quick experiments to run
- A/B test two email opens per vertical: (1) cost/economics lead vs (2) compliance/defensibility lead. Track reply rate and qualified meeting rate.
- Small calculator components (tokens->cost translated to product metric) performed surprisingly well in past tests — ship a small JS widget for each vertical landing page.
- Create 2 concise one-pagers per vertical: (1) engineering-focused (integration + metrics) (2) risk/compliance-focused (audit, keys, evidence). Keep both <1 page.

Unresolved questions / TODOs
- Need a short customer vignette for fintech showing actual checkout conversion impact; ask Solutions to produce a 1-page after next pilot (owner: Liam).
- Obtain a sanitized audit-log example from infra/product for the healthcare demo (owner: Priya).
- Validate gov/defense procurement language with legal (owner: Marco).

Quick reference copy snippets (ready for SDR body):
- Fintech: "Can I show you how we cut inference spend during peak checkout while keeping latency under 200ms?"
- Healthcare: "We help teams ship auditable inference — provenance and deployability first, accuracy second."
- Legal: "Automated redlines with attached evidence — reduce review time without losing defensibility."
- SaaS: "Swap models without swapping your product — same API, different price/latency profile."
- Gov/Def: "Private inference that fits into secure architectures — procurement-friendly, auditable, and observable."

This doc is ideation-first. Please add short notes below rather than long rewrites. If you take a section, add your initials and a 1–2 line summary of what you’ll run in the next 2 weeks.
